title: Planning and managing safe crowds
summary: Safe events are designed, informed and managed in every phase. DIM-ICE and RAMP structure the risk analysis; flow rates and egress times size the exits.
outcomes: use DIM-ICE to structure a crowd risk assessment
describe RAMP analysis: routes, areas, movement and profile
size an exit with a flow rate and an egress time
list practical measures that keep density down
narration_en: How do organisers keep crowds safe? Crowd scientist Keith Still teaches two tools. The first, DIM-ICE, crosses three things organisers control, design, information and management, with the three phases of an event, ingress, circulation and egress. Each of the nine cells is a question: is the design of the entry route adequate, does information reach people during circulation, how is egress managed? The second tool, RAMP, looks at routes, areas, movement over time, and the profile of the crowd. Then come numbers. Guidance for sports grounds in the United Kingdom, the Green Guide, gives planning flow rates of eighty two people per metre width per minute on level routes and sixty six on stepped routes, and egress times of up to eight minutes. Divide the number of people by the flow rate and the time, and you get the exit width needed. Finally, practical measures keep density down: separate flows, one-way systems, holding areas, staggered times, and stewards with clear authority to act.
narration_ar: كيف يحافظ المنظمون على سلامة الحشود؟ يدرّس عالم الحشود كيث ستيل أداتين. الأولى، DIM-ICE، تجمع بين ثلاثة أمور يتحكم فيها المنظمون، التصميم والمعلومات والإدارة، وبين المراحل الثلاث لأي فعالية، الدخول والتنقل والخروج. وكل خلية من الخلايا التسع سؤال: هل تصميم طريق الدخول كافٍ، وهل تصل المعلومات إلى الناس أثناء التنقل، وكيف يُدار الخروج؟ والأداة الثانية، RAMP، تنظر إلى الطرق والمناطق والحركة عبر الزمن وخصائص الحشد. ثم تأتي الأرقام. فالدليل الإرشادي لملاعب الرياضة في المملكة المتحدة، المعروف بالدليل الأخضر، يقدّم معدلات تدفق تخطيطية قدرها اثنان وثمانون شخصاً لكل متر من العرض في الدقيقة على الطرق المستوية، وستة وستون على الطرق المدرّجة، وأزمنة خروج تصل إلى ثماني دقائق. اقسم عدد الأشخاص على معدل التدفق والزمن، تحصل على عرض المخرج المطلوب. وأخيراً، تحافظ إجراءات عملية على انخفاض الكثافة: فصل التدفقات، وأنظمة الاتجاه الواحد، ومناطق الانتظار، والمواعيد المتدرجة، ومنظّمون لديهم صلاحية واضحة للتصرف.

tour.text: Start with DIM-ICE: what can go wrong in design, information and management, in each phase?
Then RAMP: which routes, which areas, how movement changes over time, and who the crowd is.
Choose planning flow rates and target times from the guidance that applies.

sections.heading: DIM-ICE
sections.html:
Keith Still's DIM-ICE model crosses what organisers control with the phases of an event:

IngressCirculationEgress
Designentry routes, gatesconcourses, toiletsexits, routes away
Informationtickets, signsscreens, announcementsexit signs, PA
Managementqueues, searchesstewardingstaggered release

Each cell is a question to ask. Clusters of weak cells point to where an incident is likely.

sections.heading: RAMP analysis
sections.html: RAMP asks about Routes (where people come from and go), Areas (holding and moving spaces, measured), Movement (arrival and departure profiles over time) and Profile (who the crowd is: age, culture, familiarity, purpose). A football crowd, a family festival and a pilgrimage need different plans even in the same space.

sections.heading: Sizing exits with flow rates
sections.html:
The Green Guide (6th edition) gives planning flow rates of 82 people per metre width per minute on level routes and 66 on stepped routes, and egress times of up to 8 minutes (less where fire risk is higher).

exit width = people ÷ (flow rate × egress time)

Example: 6,000 people, level route, 8 minutes: 6,000 ÷ (82 × 8) ≈ 9.1 m. Stepped route: 6,000 ÷ (66 × 8) ≈ 11.4 m. Note these are per minute, unlike the per-second specific flows of module 1.4.

sections.heading: Keeping density down on the day
sections.html: Good plans fail without good operations. Measures that work: separate in and out flows; one-way systems; holding areas and metering to release people in batches; staggered start and finish times; clear information in the crowd's languages; and stewards with the authority to stop inflow when density rises.

callouts.title: Rates are not laws of nature
callouts.html: Planning rates include safety margins and apply to the venues they were written for. Use the guidance that applies where you work, and check routes beyond the exit too.

callouts.title: Plan it
callouts.html: A stand of 4,000 needs to leave in 8 minutes by a stepped route. Width? 4,000 ÷ (66 × 8) ≈ 7.6 m.

takeaways: DIM-ICE crosses Design, Information and Management with Ingress, Circulation and Egress.
RAMP analysis looks at Routes, Areas, Movement and Profile.
Exit width = people ÷ (flow rate × egress time); the Green Guide uses 82 (level) and 66 (stepped) per metre per minute and up to 8 minutes.
On the day, separate flows, metering, information and empowered stewards keep density down.
